In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper presents a novel approach to the estimation and forecasting of the wavefield based upon a parallel Ensemble Kal-man filter and pseudospectral time propagation, and the application of this forecast in a Model Predictive Control setting for the online power take-off optimization of a WEC system.

, although the proposed control scheme is not yet able to outperform the ideal case, it is able to provide a significant increase in power takeoff over the baseline case of fixed power take-off, and that it is a step towards the implementation of real-time optimal control in WEC systems.

the proposed forecasting-based control strategy is an effective way to optimize WEC power take-off, and that this strategy is robust to errors in the prediction of the oncoming waves, as long as these errors are not too large.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this work presents an efficient and robust forecasting method for the prediction-based MPC control of WEC.

we have shown that it is possible to implement a control system that optimizes the power take-off from a WEC system in real-time, and that this is possible even with a forecast of the oncoming sea state that is imperfect.

this is a first step towards an online control strategy for WEC that is able to exploit the forecast of future wavefield information to optimize power take-off in real time, while simultaneously being able to handle uncertainties in the wavefield and the system.

, even with the current level of forecasting accuracy, the proposed control scheme can be used to significantly improve power take-off efficiency, thereby increasing the competitiveness of WEC systems.
the proposed approach is a promising way to implement real time optimization of power takeoff in wave energy conversion, with a potential for significant power improvements.
